<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|4|THE GOSPEL|CHA. I.}}</noinclude>begat {{sup|‖}} Ioseph the {{sup|‖}} husband of {{sc|Marie}}: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''de qua''.}}∷ of vvhom vvas borne {{sc|Iesvs}}, vvho is called {{sc|Christ}}.⊣

{{verse|chapter=1|verse=17}}† Therefore al the generations from Abraham vnto Dauid, fourtene generations. And from Dauid to the Transmigration of Babylon, fourtene generations. And from the Transmigration of Babylon vnto {{sc|Christ}}, fourtene generations.

{{verse|chapter=1|verse=18}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō Christmas eue. and Vpon S. Iosephs day the 19 of Marche.}}And the generation of {{sc|Christ}} vvas in this vvise. When his mother {{sc|Marie}} vvas spoused to Ioseph, before they came together, she vvas found to be vvith childe by the Holy Ghost. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=19}}† Wherevpon Ioseph, for that he vvas a iust man, & vvould not {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Deu. 24, 1.''}}* put her to open shame: vvas minded secretely to dimisse her. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=20}}† But as he vvas thus thinking, behold the Angel of our Lord appeared to him in sleepe saying: Ioseph sonne of Dauid, feare not to take {{sc|Marie}} thy vvife. for that vvhich is {{sup|‖}} borne in her, is of the Holy Ghost. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=21}}† And she shal bring forth a sonne: and thou shalt call his name {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ IESVS an Hebrue word, in English SAVIOVR.}}∷ {{sc|Iesvs}}. For he shal saue his people from their sinnes.⊣ {{verse|chapter=1|verse=22}}† And al this vvas done that it might be fulfilled vvhich our Lord spake by the Prophet saying. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=23}}† ''Behold {{sup|‖}} a Virgin shal be vvith childe, and {{sup|‖}} bring forth a sonne, and they shal call his name Emmanuel'', vvhich being interpreted is, ''God vvith vs.''{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 7, 14.''}} {{verse|chapter=1|verse=24}}† And Ioseph rising vp from sleepe, did as the Angel of our Lord cōmaunded him, and tooke his vvife. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=25}}† And he knevv her not {{sup|‖}} til she brought forth her first borne sonne: and called his name {{sc|Iesvs}}.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. I.}}}}

''3. Thamar.''] Christ abhorred not to take flesh of some that were il, as he chose Iudas among his Apostles: Let not vs disdaine to receaue our spiritual birth and sustenance of such as be not alwayes good.

''16. Ioseph.''] Ioseph marying our Lady as neere of kinne (for so was the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Nu. 36.''}}* law) by his pedegree sheweth hers, and consequently Christs pedegree from Dauid.

''16. Husband.''] True and perfect mariage, and continual liuing in the same, without carnal copulation. ''Aug. lib. 2. Consen. Euang. c.1''.

''20. Borne in her.''] The triple good or perfection of mariage accomplished in the parents of Christ, to wit, Issue, Fidelitie, Sacrament. ''Aug. de nup. & conc. li. 1. c.11''.

''23. A Virgin.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Virginitie preferred.}}Our Sauiour borne in mariage, but yet of a Virgin, would honour both states: and withal, teacheth vs agaynst Iouinian the old Heretike and these of our time, that virginity and the continent life are preferred before mariage that hath carnal copulation. ''See S. Hierom. adu. Iouin. and S. Greg. Nazianz. Ser. 20. de studio in pauperes, in initio''.

''23. A Virgin.''] As our Ladie both a virgin and a mother, brought forth Christ the head corporally: so the Churche a virgin and a mother, bringeth forth the members of this head spiritually. ''Aug. li. de virg. ca.2''.

''23. And bring forth.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Our B. Ladies perpetual virginity.}}The Heretike Iouinian is here refuted, holding that her virginity was corrupted in bringing forth Christ. ''Aug. hær. 28. Li. 1 cont. Iulian. c.2''.<noinclude>{{continues|''25. Til,''}}</noinclude>
